description: EPS root parent and proposed gap requirements. All gap items are review status and require human approval.

requirements.title: EPS System Requirements Baseline
requirements.statement: The EPS software requirements baseline shall be allocated to SWC_ElectricPowerSteering on ECU_EPS_Main and shall trace to the steering system/stakeholder requirements.
requirements.source: Placeholder parent injected by the hardening system
requirements.rationale: The source CSV has no system/stakeholder hierarchy. This placeholder enables traceability without inventing a stakeholder requirement.
open_issues: Placeholder system parent; replace with the real steering system/stakeholder requirement and confirm ASIL allocation.

requirements.title: Torque Sensor Loss Safe State
requirements.statement: When both torque-sensor channels are invalid or disagree beyond the calibrated tolerance for more than 30 ms, the EPS shall enter FAIL_SAFE and limit motor current to the calibrated limp-home value.
requirements.rationale: The source defines a plausibility check but not the both-channel-loss safe state and timing.
open_issues: 30 ms reaction and limp-home current are proposed; confirm with the EPS safety analysis.

requirements.title: Motor Position Sensor Loss
requirements.statement: When the motor position sensor is invalid for more than 20 ms, the EPS shall disable field-oriented control and enter FAIL_SAFE.
requirements.source: Gap analysis: motor control safety, ISO 26262-6
requirements.rationale: The source set does not cover loss of motor position feedback, which is required for safe torque control.
open_issues: Confirm the position-sensor interface, detection window and FAIL_SAFE reaction.

requirements.title: Vehicle Speed Signal Loss
requirements.statement: When the vehicle-speed signal is invalid or lost for more than 50 ms, the EPS shall limit assist to the calibrated limp-home value and set a CAN-timeout DTC.
requirements.rationale: The source defines CAN-timeout detection but not the assist limitation during loss of vehicle speed.
open_issues: Confirm the limp-home assist value and recovery condition after speed returns.

requirements.title: Watchdog Reset Recovery
requirements.statement: After an ECU reset caused by the hardware watchdog, the EPS shall remain in FAIL_SAFE until the startup self-test passes and the reset cause is recorded.
requirements.rationale: The source detects watchdog expiry but does not define the post-reset safe-state and recovery condition.
open_issues: Confirm the reset-cause register mapping and the self-test pass criteria.

requirements.title: Safe State per Fault Class
requirements.statement: The EPS shall map each safety-relevant fault class to a defined safe state (assist disabled, limp-home, or controlled shutdown) and shall record the active safe state in PP_EPSStatus.
requirements.source: Gap analysis: ISO 26262-6 safe state, ASPICE SWE.4
requirements.rationale: The source uses FAIL_SAFE as a single state but does not define fault-class-specific safe states.
open_issues: The fault-class-to-safe-state table must come from the safety analysis.

requirements.title: Thermal Derating to Disable Transition
requirements.statement: The EPS shall transition from thermal derating to motor disable when motor temperature exceeds 100 C and shall not re-enable assist until the temperature falls below the calibrated recovery threshold.
requirements.rationale: The source defines 80 C derating and 100 C disable but not the recovery threshold or re-enable condition.
open_issues: Confirm the recovery threshold and hysteresis with the thermal/steering-feel calibration.

requirements.title: Calibration Verification
requirements.statement: At startup and after a calibration update, the EPS shall verify that every safety-relevant calibration parameter is within its declared range and consistent with the steering variant.
requirements.rationale: The source exposes calibration parameters but does not require verification.
open_issues: Define the safety-relevant calibration list and variant matrix.

requirements.title: Steering Variant Configuration
requirements.statement: The EPS shall select its assist map, torque constant, current limit and end-stop limits from a validated steering-variant configuration.
requirements.rationale: The source uses vehicle-dependent parameters but does not define variant selection.
open_issues: Define the variant matrix and configuration source.
requirements.constraint_rationale: Configuration constraint; verified by variant-matrix review and end-of-line test.

requirements.title: Software and Calibration Update Integrity
requirements.statement: The EPS shall only accept authenticated and integrity-protected software and calibration updates and shall record a fault when verification fails.
requirements.source: Gap analysis: ISO 21434, UNECE R155/R156 context
requirements.rationale: A safety-critical steering function needs update integrity; the source set does not address cybersecurity.
open_issues: Develop the full ISO 21434 cybersecurity requirements; this is a placeholder.
requirements.constraint_rationale: Security constraint on the update path; verified by security review and update-integration test.

requirements.title: Fault Injection and Observability
requirements.statement: The EPS shall expose test hooks to inject torque-sensor loss, position-sensor loss, CAN timeout, undervoltage and overtemperature faults and shall publish the resulting mode and DTC bitmask.
requirements.source: Gap analysis: ASPICE SWE.4, ISO 26262-6 fault injection
requirements.rationale: Verification of the safety mechanisms needs controllability and observability.
open_issues: Confirm the production-disable mechanism for the test hooks.
requirements.constraint_rationale: Verification-enabling constraint; reviewed for production isolation.
